title: Native and Multiplatform Performance knowledge check

questions.prompt: Which statement best captures the main idea of “Native and Multiplatform Performance”?
options: It means all Kotlin libraries and platform APIs behave identically.
It removes the need to understand types or runtime behavior.
Kotlin Multiplatform organizes shared logic and target-specific implementations through source sets; only APIs available for every configured target belong in common code.
It makes versioning, input validation, and testing unnecessary.
questions.answer_key: Kotlin Multiplatform organizes shared logic and target-specific implementations through source sets; only APIs available for every configured target belong in common code.
questions.explanation: The reliable answer is grounded in the lesson’s main principle: Kotlin Multiplatform organizes shared logic and target-specific implementations through source sets; only APIs available for every configured target belong in common code. questions.prompt: Which learning/debugging practice is most reliable for “Native and Multiplatform Performance”?
options: Assume the compiler or toolchain is broken without reducing the example.
Use a minimal reproducible example, compare the actual result with the expected result, and check the target/version assumptions.
Change several unrelated parts at once and keep the result that looks plausible.
Ignore warnings and suppress failures before identifying the cause.
questions.answer_key: Use a minimal reproducible example, compare the actual result with the expected result, and check the target/version assumptions.
questions.explanation: A minimal reproducible example and version-aware testing separate a real behavior from a mistaken assumption. Review the example and one relevant edge case before moving on.

questions.prompt: Which claim should a learner avoid when applying “Native and Multiplatform Performance”?
options: A source-code change is an optimization even without measurements.
Never inspect the official API reference for the selected target.
Treat draft or experimental features as universally stable.
Expose every internal implementation detail to every caller.
questions.answer_key: A source-code change is an optimization even without measurements.
questions.explanation: The misconception to avoid is: A source-code change is an optimization even without measurements. Review the example and one relevant edge case before moving on.
